value.title: Unstructured search and overhead

value.summary: The six unordered two-symbol supports in {00,01,10,11} reduce to four adjacent supports and two diagonal supports. The diagonal supports split into the antirepetition pair {01,10} and the repetition pair {00,11}; singleton supports convey no information. This exhausts all super-input supports of size at most two.
value.title: Two-symbol super-input orbit reduction

value.summary: Adjacent supports discard an input-independent product coordinate and admit a cooperative binary-erasure upper bound of 1/2 bit; the antirepetition support likewise has binary-erasure receiver marginals and a 1/2-bit cooperative bound. For the repetition support, the assumed binary-input Marton theorem reduces the sum-rate to randomized time division. Concavity and reflection symmetry of its receiver-information curve, together with a tangent bound on the receiver-information difference, give a strict upper bound below 0.615 bit.
value.title: Rate bounds for the two-symbol support classes

value.summary: A Python standard-library checker constructs the product receiver marginals with exact rational arithmetic, verifies the six-support orbit classification and the adjacent, antirepetition, and repetition transition structures, and uses directed high-precision Decimal intervals to check the repetition-support tangent bound, the strict 0.615-bit endpoint, and its separation from 0.7232857688439092 bits.
value.title: Exact two-symbol orbit and tangent-certificate verifier

value.summary: Assuming the Geng--Jog--Nair--Wang binary-input Marton theorem, every finite Marton law for the half-skew BSSC product channel whose induced super-input is supported on at most two of the four symbols has sum-rate strictly below 0.615 bit. Since product randomized time division exceeds 0.7232857688439092 bits, any strict two-letter Marton improvement over the current BSSC achievable rate must use at least three super-input symbols. The result does not exclude gains on three- or four-symbol support.
value.title: Two-letter Marton two-symbol support pruning

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted support-pruning theorem and its supporting reduction, proof, and verifier directly advance the durable non-root objective of determining the structures required for a multiletter Marton gain on the BSSC.
